rv.q: With these two actors, it makes you feel complicit as you watch and laugh at this ersatz Lincoln and Booth performing their sad-sack realities for your pleasure and enjoyment.
Topdog/Underdog feels classic Steppenwolf but also contemporary and gripping.

This is an intense and ultimately very moving, Broadway-caliber show in relatively intimate environs with a special pair of actors, a director who can make 2001 feel like yesterday and a play that casts new shadows every time it's encountered.
This needs to be said: the chemistry between two great actors is palpable and consistent.
It’s a must‑see: a clear, confident, and emotionally charged production of a modern classic, staged by artists who understand both the intimacy of the play and the mythic weight beneath it.
This is a stellar rendition of this complicated tale.
For anyone looking for a production that is both entertaining and emotionally challenging, Topdog/Underdog delivers.
Leon’s careful direction lets Davis and Smallwood really make these characters their own, leaning into elements that made this feel like a first-time viewing for me.
What I do know is that Leon’s production made me see Topdog/Underdog differently, turning our act of watching into part of the play’s unsettling equation.

Leon’s production and the two actors at its heart flesh out the childhood trauma, lost hopes, and desperate dreams of beating the big con game at the center of American life that bring these brothers together and eventually tear them apart.
Ultimately, Topdog/Underdog remains a remarkable piece of American theatre because Parks refuses to let history stay in the past.
A quarter-century after its debut, Topdog/Underdog still has something to say.
It’s a funny, intellectual and gut-wrenching experience that should not be missed.

At one time, Lincoln was a hustler who had great skill at the game called "three-card monte", a street con game that at one time was played to con tourists in major cities. He no longer does this, but Booth, has been trying to master the game so that he can be "the man".

cn.t: Critics hail this Steppenwolf revival as a blistering, captivating production of Parks' Pulitzer-winning masterpiece, with Davis and Smallwood delivering dazzling performances in a timeless American tragedy about brotherhood and broken dreams.
